ROOT_CAUSE.summary: PID 7044 received an orderly GUI Editor quit request while the second asynchronous MCP test job was still running. The Editor performed a graceful shutdown sequence, but neither Editor.log nor Windows process-audit data records the identity of the requester. External/manual close or an external WM_CLOSE-equivalent request is therefore the most likely classification. A Unity crash, OOM, test timeout, MCP/API wrapper timeout, and wrapper child-process kill are not supported by the evidence.

second_full_regression.pid_7044_exit_code_reason: The MCP call attached to an already-running GUI Editor launched by Unity Hub and returned asynchronously. It did not own or wait a process handle. Windows process termination auditing and Sysmon were unavailable, and Editor.log did not print a return code for this exit.

timeouts_and_waits.timeout_assessment: No global full-regression execution limit below 1800 seconds was configured. The only wait spanning the run was the 2400-second read-only monitor, which was not reached. Values below 1800 seconds were initialization, transport, relay, or per-test limits and did not cap total suite duration. A future global limit below 1800 seconds would be inadequate because prior complete runs took 1545.1287735 and 1690.6510323 seconds.

duration_comparison.recommendation_basis: 3600 seconds is more than twice the slower complete run and leaves headroom for asset refresh, result writing, and shutdown without treating normal long tests as hung.

required_execution_setting_changes: Do not use an asynchronously attached GUI Editor as the final acceptance process if its exit code and ownership must be auditable.
Use one dedicated process-owned batchmode/EditMode invocation that writes focused_results.xml directly and returns a retained process exit code.
Set the global process and wrapper wait limit to at least 3600 seconds; never below 1800 seconds.
Keep the MCP initialization timeout separate from the full-run timeout; 120000 ms remains an initialization-only value.
Prevent GUI close, Unity Hub project close, sleep/logoff, MCP reconnect, and test-status polling for the entire run and result-writer shutdown window.
Preserve the existing contaminated and isolated-recheck XML files exactly as they are.
